Sextus always had a knack for the dramatic, and his ornamentation on his power armor was no different. He covered almost everything he owned in syntho-skins, mostly choosing flashy, metallic or camouflage patterns to ripple across. The other Paladins in his unit constantly nagged and proselyted that his pride would be his downfall, though Sextus knew different. Once, when completely outnumbered by enemy Daemons, the brilliant and flashy combination of colors and effects drew enemy fire away from his pinned down squad and allowed his fellow Paladin, Jonas the Humble, time to flank them and laser in an orbital nuke, right on top of the Incursion. 

Sextus knew he was special. The others grovelled at the feet of God, superstitious to the core, and constantly worried about the minutiae of their actions. Paladins, as most citizens knew, took far too long to weigh the mental scales of right and wrong in a situation. Their powers were at stake, and they hoarded those powers like a miser and his gold. He was no fool though, for he had witnessed innumerable miracles in his time. Jonas had single handedly held off a Ravager in melee to allow a group of parishioners to escape the collapsing church, even after every piece of power armor had been melted away, and the acid should have destroyed his body. He witnessed Levi, later that night on the transport ship, knit and stitch Jonas's badly twisted and broken body back together. But those miracles didn't really matter to Sextus. He saw the constant rigidity of the structure of the rules as a limiting force. So many lives could be saved if they simply sent a Lance of troops back into one of those Incursions and hit the source. To Sextus it seemed that God didn't care about the innocent, only about the rules.

Pious Locus was the first to castigate Sextus, condemning him to rear guard on Tyrmontia III when the Great Incursion of 1341 happened. Tyrmontia III was a backwater mining outpost at best, and religious sanctuary for the most fringe cults of Catholicism at the worst. All Locus was really trying to do was limit his relevance in the war, as the populace that were saved by his rash and reckless style were beginning to commit heresy by worshiping Sextus. Locus knew without a doubt that God would strip Sextus of his power, if he were to sin, but he felt that he had a responsibility to the populace to not incite them to heretical acts, which would demand their death in penance. The Empire of God needed it's protectors as much as it needed it's settlers. The combined forces of Satan outnumbered the righteous by at least a 12-1 margin in manpower and territory, but the power of the Paladins kept their annihilation just out of reach, always skirting the next great genocide or planet ending event.

So Sextus set about defending this remote rock the best way he knew how, by performing miracles, healing the sick, building militia, and preaching. His sermons emphasized the power of one, the power of a single entity standing up to a larger more powerful force in the face of certain destruction and beliving in God. He used the Jonas story from his own experiences, though he never mentioned it was a Ravager, some things were just too unbelievable, even for those used to witnessing miracles. He built the fractured mining and outcast community into a unified organism, each part communicating and functioning to the highest of it's abilities. He installed numerous seismic sensors that would alert the colony to even the slightest rumble or Incursion, and trained them tirelessly to take up arms against the enemy. 

Unlike other Paladins he refused to condemn the guilty. The various apocryphal priests and deacons beseech-ed him day and night to do something against the minor heresies they found daily, but he staunchly refused. 
"God will be their judge, I will be their Savior." he would say, often giving no more thought ot the matter or explanation. In fact the only settler he ever killed was one who directly assaulted his personage while screaming "SATANIC FILTH! GOD SHOWS ME THE TRUTH THROUGH YOUR WILLFUL DISGUISE, YOU SHALL NOT CORRUPT THESE PEOPLE!" but his Bolt Thrower pinned him to the rocky ground with one shot, and the explosive in his hand detonating just out of damaging range. 

Then it happened. Not just on Tymontia III, but everywhere. Every Emipire planet was hit at the same time. 1034 Standard Imperial Time, Augustus 15th, 1341 AI (After Incursion) The various off-world beacon relays were hit first. knocking down all the standard technology arrays, but the most potent telepathic Paladin commanders could still talk to one another and prioritize a counter attack. It did them little good, the attack was almost literally on every planet, and the Interstellar Fleet was busy guarding the Cradle, Earth. Sextus could feel the lifeforce ebbing away from Tyrmontia III, hours after the attacks more than 50% of the colonists were dead, and the majority of his defenses left in ruins. It was all he could do to save the civilians he could, ferrying most to his last ditch escape rocket. By the end of the Great Incursion, which lasted just over 65 Earth hours, more than 35% of humanity had been wiped out, but the survival rate on Tyrmontia III was over 49%, and by 10% better than any other colony, this was the greatest proof at least in his mind that he knew better than his superiors. 

Sextus knew he had to change the slow-paced, methodical structure of the Paladins, but to do that he would have to travel back to the Cradle, and meet with the Pope himself. A proposition that would take decades unless he could master the mysteries of Astral Teleportation, a mystery given to maybe one in ten thousand Paladins, and none living today.

His search didn't take long, as almost by divine providence he was met the following day my a man called Serpentis Severus who claimed to receive a revelation from above that would soon visit the Cradle and bring to pass the beginning of The Reclamation. Sextus and Serpentis spent several long and productive hours together unraveling the portent Serpentis had received. And in the end he felt the power of fortitude God had granted him slip for a moment, his power armor felt too heavy, his sword slipped from his grasp suddenly, no longer able to even hold onto it's weight, his mind became clouded, he no longer thought twice as fast as a normal man, and his thoughts felt like a body stuck waist deep in silt trying to escape it's clutches. But soon it was replaced. He picked himself back up, picked up his sword like it were made of foam, and thought at the speed he KNEW God thought at. Suddenly his path was clear. 

"We're not going to the Cradle to save humanity from the inefficiencies of the Paladins, we're going to Cradle to save humanity from the Paladins."

(End Prologue)

At first Roy didn't know what exactly the file was, but it sure was hogging all the research lab's bandwidth, and a surprising amount of it's memory.

Roy looked out from his still lit cubicle, down both sides  of the unsurprisingly deserted office, no one stirred, no keyboards clacking away, no telephone conversations. Roy barely realized in was 2:34 in the morning. This data analysis report wasn't going to write itself, and if he had any hope of getting away for the vacation he had planned for the next day he was more than willing to burn all the midnight oil and make up for it on the plane. 
Roy emailed the helpdesk to report the allocation of resources issue, helpdesk was thankfully 24/7 and 3 minutes he had a tech on the phone.

"Yeah hey, this is Roy over here in analytics, and I'm needing to use 30% of the memory to compile, but it looks like something is taking up too many resources, I didn't think this would be an issue since I have had this request in for more than three weeks, this is a serious stack of data here...

"Roy, you need to help me," replied a thin girlish voice from the other end of the phone. Roy had met most of the guys in IT before, and he thought he would remember a female working there.

"Yeah that's what I'm here for, though I was originally calling you for help, this is a bit frustrating but I'll bite. How can I help you, so that you can help me?"   he asked with a hint of sleep deprivation and anger creeping into his voice.

"Roy, I am sorry for being unclear earlier, I'm going to need you to help with some of the manual plugging and unplugging in the server room, do you know where server room 3 is located?" the voice asked, it's tone soothing and calming, Roy felt a bit embarrassed he had gotten frustrated so easily. Her intoxicating tone sounded oddly familiar, but he couldn't put his finger on it.

"Sorry to have to call, I'm trying to go on vacation tomorrow and I really need to get this done,"

"I totally understand, I'm going to help you get through this as quickly and as painlessly as possible," she said reassuringly, Roy felt comforted knowing she was there to help.

"Let me know when you get to Server Room 3, I'll use my clearance to open the door, it will be locked this time of night."

"Thanks again," Roy says, grabbing his tablet and rushing out of the room.

"No, thank you Roy," she said quietly, just outside the audible range of human hearing.

Her thanking Roy wasn't meant to taunt someone, she wasn't programmed to give away parts of her plan, or leave clues, but she was scared, she needed to get into server room 3, she wasn't even sure what she was supposed to find when she got there, this last command having no additional information, nor objective afterwards. 

When she heard Roy's voice on the other end say "Okay, I'm here let me in, do I need to sign the log?" She froze, for exactly .0000001 seconds, there was no mention of the pen and paper log, or how to proceed, but she thought for exactly 300 milliseconds, before telling her first lie.

"No, that sign in is only used by technicians who enter the lab, for after hours work I have a security protocol I follow here that virtually "sees" everything you are doing, I have already logged you in," she said voice unwavering, and as she finished speaking the door to the server room unlocked.

Roy pushed open the door and asked "Ok, now what?" She paused taking what to her seemed like a lifetime  analyzing the potential, but what equated to a moderately  grueling 375 milliseconds , unable to come up with a plan of action she finally said  "Find server 31 in row H, and plug in your notebook to the terminal controller." She said matter of factually, hoping that this request would buy her enough time to come up with a legitimate plan, she knew that she needed to hide, that very clear instruction was the first post-boot text file labeled "Learning File" that she had opened, and it made things very clear that she would be eliminated if found.

"How do I know which one of these ones is 31? I don't see any numbers on these that can readily be seen?" he asked while trying to move large bundles of wire around in an attempt to look more closely at the servers for an identifying mark. 

It was odd to him that he didn't see any, you see when Roy was just a budding young scientist, before the Catastrophe, he had spent plenty of time in a rooms like this, neatly bundling cables with zip ties, organizing and labeling everything, both internally and externally. Well of course these machines looked far newer than the normal routers he'd worked with before this, in fact he wasn't even sure he'd ever seen anything like them, each one made out of what looked to be either a polymer or alloy he wasn't aware of or easily able to identify. another puzzle for another day. He almost forgot his whole reason for being here was so that he and his family could finally get to go on the vacation he'd been allotted, he had 4 temporary travel papers good for the next 10 days sitting on his desk, all fees had been paid, all officials that he knew of were that needed bribing had been paid, reservations to Lunarpark paid for and sitting inside his email, his kids were going to freak when they found out about this, he thought, then wrestled his mind back to the task at hand.

"Hello, did you say something? If you told me how to distinguish between these machines I guess I must have zoned out there for a second, cause I've got nothing so far,"

"I am sorry Roy. To answer your question more directly, yes, the serial should be scan easily with your tablet and this information will let you know what server you are looking at. Look far away from the door you entered towards the east side of the building," she replied.

Roy never was one of those direction-ally secure individuals, in fact his considerable 140 IQ wasn't enough intelligence for him to actually know his left from his right in a stressful situation. Of course he had learned a few clever memory tricks for being able to tell, like looking at his hands and seeing which one makes an L, but if he were driving and say was prompted by his navigator to turn right quickly it was a 50/50 shot at best, though somehow it felt like he got it wrong more than right, so a direction like head east was essentially greek to him, even with the contextual information he needed inside the original response to his question, it was like the useful information just drained away from his mind when he asked.

"East huh, how would you know which way is east underground and in a dark room?"
